summary: Practise forensic audit scoping, transaction screening and evidence-linked reporting. Explore the five-day course and its applied case exercises.
lede: Forensic auditing gives audit, accounting and compliance professionals a structured way to examine suspected fraud and document findings. Participants practise allegation triage and audit scoping, screen transaction data with Benford’s Law in Excel, and maintain traceable evidence records. They also plan interviews and draft evidence-linked findings that distinguish supported conclusions from limitations in the available records.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course suits professionals who already work with audit, accounting, compliance or investigation records and need a disciplined way to examine suspected fraud. It is designed for roles that make, document or review forensic audit decisions.
prerequisites: Working knowledge of internal audit, accounting, compliance or investigation records is expected. No coding is required. Bring a laptop with Excel installed for the transaction-screening exercise; the exercise uses a sample transaction extract.
